title: The branch always wins
prompt:
# Story 3: The branch always wins

- **Story**: XXX-branch-wins
- **Created**: 2026-11-27
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open story 003 in two browsers (two people); in the first, change the story, save and sync; in the second, within 30 seconds,
  see the story replaced and the notice "Updated from story-003 and saved."; reload the second browser and see the new text is stored.

## Story

As a team member, I want what was pushed to the branch of the story I have open to replace my copy and be saved straight away, so that
when two of us touch the same story we never have a conflict to solve: the last push is the story.

## Acceptance tests

Noticing a push

- [ ] **Given** a story or enabler is open and GitHub is connected, **Then** BWYN looks at the head of its branch every 30 seconds, and at
  once when the window is used again.
- [ ] **Given** the head is the commit this machine last pulled or pushed, **Then** nothing happens.
- [ ] **Given** the head is another commit, **Then** BWYN downloads the document's files from the branch, replaces the open document with
  them, saves it in the database, and remembers the head as the last commit it knows.
- [ ] **Given** the document has no open branch, **Then** BWYN watches the base branch the same way, for the document's own files.

Replacing

- [ ] **Given** the branch changed the text, the meta.json, a diagram or the UI example, **Then** each of them is replaced here, the screen
  shows the new version, and the Diagrams button shows the diagrams the story now holds.
- [ ] **Given** a file of the document was deleted on the branch (for example the class diagram), **Then** it is deleted here too.
- [ ] **Given** the story is in another theme folder on the branch, **Then** it moves to that theme here.
- [ ] **Given** the replace worked, **Then** a notice under the header says "Updated from story-003 and saved." and names the files, for
  example "story.md, diagrams/sequence.mmd".
- [ ] **Given** the user had unsaved changes in the text, **Then** they are replaced too, and the notice adds "Your unsaved changes were
  replaced."
- [ ] **Given** a diagram or UI dialog was open, **Then** it closes, and the notice says so.
- [ ] **Given** the page is reloaded after a replace, **Then** the new version is what shows: it was saved in the database.

Never a conflict

- [ ] **Given** the same file changed here and on the branch, **Then** the branch's version is kept and no conflict is shown.
- [ ] **Given** a story that is not open, **Then** nothing is pulled for it until it is opened. **When** it is opened, **Then** its branch
  is looked at at once.
- [ ] **Given** GitHub cannot be reached, **Then** nothing changes here and BWYN tries again at the next look.

## Business rules and constraints

- **What is fetched always overwrites what is here.** There is no merge, no conflict and no Force pull for a story or an enabler.
- **What is fetched is saved in the database at once.** The user does not press Save after a pull.
- **The last commit known is remembered per machine**, so a push from this machine is never pulled back as if it were a teammate's.
- **One person per branch is the way of working.** When two work on the same document, the one who pushed last wins and the other's copy
  is replaced.

## Out of scope

- Telling who pushed, or showing what changed (a diff).
- Keeping the replaced version anywhere to bring it back.
- Pulling documents that are not open.

## Tasks

- [ ] Poll the head of the open document's branch (or of the base branch when it has none) every 30 seconds and when the window is used
  again.
- [ ] On a new head, download the document's files, replace them here (deleted files too, the theme folder too) and save them in the
  database.
- [ ] Remember the head as the last commit known for the document.
- [ ] Show the notice, with the files and the unsaved changes that were replaced.
- [ ] Remove conflicts, waiting and Force pull from the sync of stories and enablers.
- [ ] Test a push from another machine, unsaved changes, a deleted diagram, a moved story, and a push from this machine that is not
  pulled back.

tasks.text: Add a backend outbound port `BranchHeadPort` with a method that returns the current head commit SHA for a given document's branch (or the base branch when the document has no open branch), implemented in the infrastructure layer as a GitHub API call (ADR-0017)

Add a backend application-layer command handler `PullDocumentFromBranchHandler` that calls `BranchHeadPort`, compares the returned SHA with the stored last-known SHA, downloads changed and deleted files when they differ, persists the new content, updates the last-known SHA, and returns the list of affected files
Add a Flyway migration that adds a `last_known_branch_sha` column (per document per installation) to the relevant table (ADR-0010)

Expose a `POST /projects/{projectId}/documents/{documentId}/pull-if-changed` endpoint in `bwyn-rest` that delegates to the handler and returns the list of replaced files and a flag for whether unsaved changes were present (ADR-0014, ADR-0017)
Write ArchUnit tests asserting that `BranchHeadPort` lives in the domain layer and its implementation lives in the infrastructure layer (ADR-0009)
Write a Testcontainers integration test for the pull handler covering: head unchanged (no-op), head changed with file updates, head changed with a deleted file, and GitHub unreachable (ADR-0012)
In the frontend ViewModel, add a polling effect that calls the pull endpoint every 30 seconds and immediately when the window regains focus, and exposes a `replaceNotice` observable (ADR-0007)

In the frontend ViewModel, handle the response: update the document state, close any open diagram or UI-example dialog, and set the notice text including the file list and the unsaved-changes warning when applicable
Render the notice below the document header in the React component; dismiss it when the user navigates away (ADR-0007)
Remove the conflict dialog, the "waiting" state, and the "Force pull" action from the story and enabler sync flow established in story 048

Write Jest unit tests for the ViewModel covering: no-op on matching SHA, replace with file list, replace with deleted file, replace with theme move, unsaved-changes warning, dialog close, and GitHub-unreachable no-op (ADR-0005, Principle: UI/Front end Tests pay only for what they assert)
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build, Practice: Continuous Integration)

Add a Flyway migration that adds a `last_known_branch_sha` column (per document per installation) to the relevant table (ADR-0010) _(Not needed: `git_document_sync.last_known_head` already exists from `V23__keep_document_branches.sql`.)_

Expose a `POST /projects/{projectId}/documents/{documentId}/pull-if-changed` endpoint in `bwyn-rest` that delegates to the handler and returns the list of replaced files and a flag for whether unsaved changes were present (ADR-0014, ADR-0017) _(As `POST /api/projects/{projectId}/git/{kind}/{id}/pull`; it returns the replaced files. Unsaved changes are only known in the browser, so the backend returns no flag for them.)_
